content: 1. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of sildenafil by inhibiting its metabolism through the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Similarly, ritonavir also increases sildenafil levels or effects via the same mechanism. It is recommended to avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is necessary, monitor for toxicities. Patients receiving indinavir with ritonavir should not exceed 25 mg of sildenafil for erectile dysfunction treatment within a 48-hour period. For other protease inhibitors, a lower initial sildenafil dose of 25 mg is advised. Sildenafil use for pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) with ritonavir is not recommended. 2. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of silodosin by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. This combination is contraindicated. 3. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of siponimod by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Both siponimod and lopinavir prolong the QTc interval, necessitating caution. Co-administration of siponimod with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors plus moderate or strong CYP2C9 inhibitors is not recommended. 4. Lopinavir and ritonavir increase the levels or effects of sirolimus by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. This combination is contraindicated. 5. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of sofpironium topical by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP2D6. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Concomitant use of sofpironium with strong CYP2D6 inhibitors may increase sofpironium levels and the risk of adverse effects. 6. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of solifenacin by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Both solifenacin and lopinavir prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 7. Ritonavir and lopinavir increase the levels or effects of sonidegib by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Co-administration of sonidegib with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is not recommended. 8. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of sorafenib by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 9. Ritonavir decreases the levels or effects of sotagliflozin by inducing its metabolism through glucuronidation (UGT1A9). Avoid or use an alternative drug. Co-administration with UGT1A9 inducers may reduce sotagliflozin exposure and efficacy. 10. Sotrasib decreases ritonavir levels or effects by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, refer to the prescribing information for dosage adjustments. 11. Lopinavir and ritonavir increase the toxicity of sparsentan through pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, interrupt sparsentan treatment. When resuming sparsentan, consider dose titration. 12. St. John’s Wort decreases lopinavir and ritonavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 13. Ritonavir and lopinavir increase the levels or effects of stiripentol by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 14. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of sulbactam/durlobactam by inhibiting active secretion via OATP1. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Inhibition of OATP1 may increase sulbactam plasma concentrations. 15. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of sunitinib by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Both sunitinib and lopinavir prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 16. Lopinavir and ritonavir increase the levels or effects of suvorexant by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Suvorexant is not recommended with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 17. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of tacrolimus by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Both tacrolimus and lopinavir prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 18. Ritonavir and lopinavir increase the levels or effects of tadalafil by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Stop tadalafil at least 24 hours before initiating protease inhibitors (PIs), restart 7 days after PI initiation at 20 mg once daily, and increase to 40 mg once daily based on tolerability. 19. Ritonavir and lopinavir increase the levels or effects of tamoxifen by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Avoid or use an alternative drug. CYP3A4 inhibition reduces the conversion of tamoxifen to its active metabolite, N-desmethyl tamoxifen. 20. Lopinavir and ritonavir increase the levels or effects of tamsulosin by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 21. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of tazemetostat by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is not recommended. 22. Tepotinib increases ritonavir levels or effects by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the P-gp substrate dosage as recommended in its product labeling. 23. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of temsirolimus by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 24. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of thioridazine by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP2D6. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 25. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of tiagabine by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 26. Tipranavir decreases lopinavir levels through an unspecified mechanism, while lopinavir increases tipranavir levels by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. This combination is contraindicated. 27. Lopinavir and ritonavir increase the levels or effects of tofacitinib by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Reduce the tofacitinib dose to 5 mg once daily when co-administered with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors. 28. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of tolterodine by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 29. Ritonavir and lopinavir increase the levels or effects of tolvaptan by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. This combination is contraindicated. 30. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of topotecan by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Avoid or use an alternative drug. For oral topotecan, avoid concomitant use of P-gp inhibitors. The interaction with IV topotecan may be less severe but still clinically significant. 31. Lopinavir and ritonavir increase the levels or effects of trabectedin by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor must be used, administer it 1 week after trabectedin infusion and discontinue it the day prior to the next infusion. 32. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of trazodone by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 33. Ritonavir increases the levels of triazolam by decreasing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 34. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of trimethoprim by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 35. Triptorelin increases lopinavir toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. This combination increases the risk of torsades de pointes. 36. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of tucatinib by an unspecified mechanism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Tucatinib increases lopinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid concomitant use of tucatinib with CYP3A substrates, as minimal concentration changes may lead to serious or life-threatening toxicities. If unavoidable, reduce the CYP3A substrate dose according to product labeling. 37. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of ulipristal by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. This combination is contraindicated. 38. Vemurafenib and ritonavir both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Ritonavir increases vemurafenib levels by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. 39. Lopinavir increases the toxicity of umeclidinium bromide/vilanterol inhaled by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Exercise extreme caution when vilanterol is co-administered with drugs that prolong the QTc interval, as adrenergic agonist effects on the cardiovascular system may be potentiated. 40. Lopinavir and vandetanib both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Lopinavir increases vandetanib levels by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. 41. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of vemurafenib by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 42. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of verapamil by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 43. Lopinavir increases the toxicity of vilanterol/fluticasone furoate inhaled by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Exercise extreme caution when vilanterol is co-administered with drugs that prolong the QTc interval, as adrenergic agonist effects on the cardiovascular system may be potentiated. 44. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of vilazodone by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase vilazodone plasma levels by 50%. Reduce the daily dose to 20 mg. 45. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of vinblastine by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 46. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of vorapaxar by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 47. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of vincristine by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 48. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of vincristine liposomal by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 49. Ritonavir and lopinavir increase the levels or effects of voriconazole by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. This combination is contraindicated. 50. Vorinostat and lopinavir both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 51. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of vortioxetine by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP2D6. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Decrease the vortioxetine dose by 50% when co-administered with strong CYP2D6 inhibitors. 52. Ritonavir and abacavir both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 53. Lopinavir and ritonavir increase the levels or effects of abemaciclib by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increase plasma levels of abemaciclib and its metabolites, necessitating dose reduction. If the strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is discontinued, increase abemaciclib to the dose prior to initiating the inhibitor. 54. Lopinavir decreases the effects of acarbose through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution.
